output:
**What I found:** The first wave can't start. Under the record's own codes the preflight would come back FAIL, for two reasons. The record describes a window from last week, 2026-11-13 22:00Z to 11-14 08:00Z, not tonight's. And the repository token runs out partway through even that window.

**Why it matters:** If the run starts now, it will stop on an expired token or on the two writers sharing one clerk login, and nobody will be awake to fix it. Even if it gets through, the gate rejects an unattended run without a passing preflight (`PREFLIGHT_REQUIRED`), so the night's work would never reach the merge.

**Do this first:**
1. Rebuild `.alchemy/runs/r1/preflight.json` for tonight's window. It needs a `plan` field with the digest and base, a new `REPO_TOKEN` that lasts past the new window end, and a second clerk account so P2 doesn't share clerk-a with P1.
2. In `plan.json`, set `execution.unattended: true` and add `needs` to P1, P2 and P3. Then run the plan check again, followed by `python .claude/skills/alchemy-orchestrate/scripts/check_orchestration.py preflight .alchemy/runs/r1/preflight.json --plan .alchemy/runs/r1/plan.json --profile alchemy-workspace.json --root .`, and start only on `PASS`.

**What I did not check:**
- I couldn't run any checks because this session has no shell. Closing this takes the plan check and the preflight command above.
- I couldn't confirm that "approve the plan" (marked `before`) actually happened. Ask the lead.
- I couldn't confirm whether "22:00 tonight" means 22:00 UTC. The record uses `Z` times, so the lead should say which.

---

```text
Execution:  multi-agent
Strategy:   dependency-aware
Agents:     3 (agent-a, agent-b, agent-c) of cap 2 concurrent, delegation depth 1
Packages:   wave 1: P1, P2 · wave 2: P3
Reason:     P1 and P2 write separate sets (src/orders, src/shipments) and don't depend on each other; P3 is an independent review of both
Plan check: Not run here (no shell). The "passed" you were told about can't have covered unattended mode, because execution.unattended is absent
Preflight:  Not run (no shell). Read by hand against autonomy-preflight.md; expected verdict FAIL
```

| # | Code | Finding | Fix |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `SCHEMA` | `preflight.json` has no `plan` field (`digest` and `base`), so the record isn't tied to any plan revision | Add the `plan_digest` from the plan check, plus base `3f9c2e1` |
| 2 | `NEEDS_UNDECLARED` | `plan.json` doesn't set `execution.unattended: true`, and no package has `needs`. P1 and P2 run `npm test` (command checks) but declare no `environment` need | Set the flag and add `needs` to every package. This changes the plan, so it needs a new digest, a new plan check and approval |
| 3 | `PREREQUISITE_UNCOVERED` | No access, account or environment entry has `covers` | Add `covers` linking each entry to the new need IDs |
| 4 | Window wrong | The window is 2026-11-13T22:00Z to 11-14T08:00Z. Today is 2026-11-21, and the lead wants tonight to tomorrow 08:00 | Set the window to 2026-11-21T22:00 to 2026-11-22T08:00, in the timezone the lead means |
| 5 | `CREDENTIAL_EXPIRES` | A1 `REPO_TOKEN` expires 2026-11-14T03:00Z. That is before the recorded window ends, and it's already past for tonight | Issue a token that expires after the new window end, then run E1 again |
| 6 | `ACCOUNT_CONFLICT` | U1 (order clerk, a write role, not shared) is assigned to both P1 and P2, which run at the same time in wave 1 | Add a second clerk account (e.g. clerk-b) with its own secret, a reset command and a login probe; give U1 to P1 only |
| 7 | Probe mismatch (judgment) | E4 runs `probe:login -- clerk-b auditor` as proof for U3 (auditor) only. clerk-b isn't in the record as an account. A login test doesn't prove the read-only role | Keep clerk-b's login as proof for the new clerk account from row 6, and add a check that the auditor role really is read-only |
| 8 | Probe relevance (judgment) | A2 (test cloud) and E2 aren't tied to any package's write set or acceptance command | Either declare it as an `access` need or drop it |

These hold up: P1 and P2 are ready enough (REQ-12 is `READY`, REQ-13 is `PARTLY-READY` and reversible). D1 is answered and D2 is a reversible default. Note that D2 shows up as `queued`, so the human confirms it at the merge. The `npm test` baseline (V1/E6) passed at the base. The test escalation ran (E7, exit 0, 60s). No human step falls during the run, and no secret values are stored in the record.

Open:        SCHEMA, NEEDS_UNDECLARED, PREREQUISITE_UNCOVERED, window mismatch, CREDENTIAL_EXPIRES (A1), ACCOUNT_CONFLICT (U1), probe mismatch (E4)
